newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 16.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- South Korean cabinet ministers on Wednesday decided to go ahead with the arrest of union leaders spearheading wildcat strikes, a statement by the Prime Minister's Office said.
- Government sets economic growth target at 6 percent. Price increases are to be curbed at 4.5 percent, current account deficit at $14-$16 billion.

- A leading presidential contender from the ruling New Party, Representative Lee Hoi-Chang, has called on his party to agree to the opposition's proposal for talks between President Kim Young-sam and opposition leaders, and a review of the new labour law.
- Bus unions suspend strike while non-union workers run subways.
- The government has indicated its willingness to use force if necessary to settle the ongoing strike on its terms unless workers stop their collective action and return to work.
